title: Nehemiah 12:44–47
context: On the day of dedication, men are appointed over the storerooms for offerings, first fruits, and tithes, so that the portions the law assigns to the priests and Levites are gathered in. The priests, Levites, singers, and gatekeepers serve according to the commandment of David and Solomon, and all Israel gives the portions for the singers, gatekeepers, Levites, and priests. Both traditions read this as shared ground on supporting those who serve in worship, recalling the pledge of Nehemiah 10:35–39.

verses.text: On that day, men were appointed over the rooms for the treasures, for the wave offerings, for the first fruits, and for the tithes, to gather into them according to the fields of the cities the portions appointed by the law for the priests and Levites; for Judah rejoiced for the priests and for the Levites who served.
verses.arminianNotes:
Men are appointed “over the rooms for the treasures, for the wave offerings, for the first fruits, and for the tithes.” Arminian readers note that the people’s joy leads to practical provision.

“Judah rejoiced for the priests and for the Levites who served.”
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers see the fulfillment of the pledge in Nehemiah 10:35–39.

Both traditions treat this as shared ground: supporting those who serve in worship is part of covenant faithfulness.

verses.text: They performed the duty of their God and the duty of the purification, and so did the singers and the gatekeepers, according to the commandment of David and of Solomon his son.
verses.arminianNotes:
“They performed the duty of their God and the duty of the purification, and so did the singers and the gatekeepers, according to the commandment of David and of Solomon his son.” Arminian readers note the faithful performance of duties.

The pattern traces back to David and Solomon (cf. 2 Chr 8:14).
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers see worship ordered according to an inherited pattern.

Both traditions treat this as shared ground: faithful service follows the order God’s people received.

verses.text: For in the days of David and Asaph of old there was a chief of the singers, and songs of praise and thanksgiving to God.
verses.arminianNotes:
“For in the days of David and Asaph of old there was a chief of the singers, and songs of praise and thanksgiving to God.” Arminian readers note the appeal to the example of David’s time (cf. 1 Chr 16:7).

Praise has deep roots in Israel’s worship.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers see continuity with the worship of David’s day.

Both traditions treat this as shared ground: songs of praise and thanksgiving remain central to the worship of God’s people.

verses.text: All Israel in the days of Zerubbabel and in the days of Nehemiah gave the portions of the singers and the gatekeepers, as every day required; and they set apart that which was for the Levites; and the Levites set apart that which was for the sons of Aaron.
verses.arminianNotes:
“All Israel in the days of Zerubbabel and in the days of Nehemiah gave the portions of the singers and the gatekeepers, as every day required.” Arminian readers note the people’s ongoing faithfulness in giving.

The Levites in turn set apart a portion for the priests (cf. Num 18:26).
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers see an orderly system of provision for those who serve.

Both traditions treat this as shared ground: the section presents a positive picture that chapter 13 will show was hard to sustain.
